learning_results:
The unified recurrent controller learned useful current and robot actions, but **it did not qualify for deployment**. Its slightly better worst peak on the 700-case nominal grid did not transfer reliably to fresh conditions or prolonged motion. The deterministic controller remains the stronger prototype starting point; even that controller needs more margin and timing verification.

**Question.** Can one history-based policy control the complete flange while maintaining workpiece-normal force within ±0.5 N and managing delayed robot recentering? The experiment used one shared, two-layer, 32-state Puffer minGRU with causal force, acceleration, relative position, identified parameters and already-issued robot commands. It received no future bump profile. Its two outputs commanded coil current and robot correction through the unchanged native current driver, stability gate, delay and limits. There was no dynamic PI force controller underneath the learned current action.

**Training and selection.** Physics-informed initialization supplied force balance and causal filter features. Whole-episode evolutionary rewards adjusted successive compact parameter sets, including recurrent readouts; this was not teacher-action imitation or learning from a blank network. The stored network contains 8,101 trainable parameters, while individual evolutionary stages optimized 12, 28, 55, 41 or 37 degrees of freedom. These counts must not be confused.

The evolutionary lane completed 124 generations on the earlier sensor configuration and one generation after the budget-sensor change: **17,728 training episodes and 480,771,873 actor decisions**. The earlier stage executed 20,104 episodes including its selection and audit runs, plus 368 physics-initialization comparisons and 38 implementation checks; 21 evolutionary training episodes and three initialization comparisons physically failed. These counts exclude the separately recorded PPO experiments. The budget stage executed 616 scored episodes: 424 evolutionary training/selection/audit episodes, 136 bootstrap comparisons and 56 paired transfer-screen episodes. Five physical failures occurred in the latter two groups; the single budget evolutionary generation had none. Recovery replays remain separate from optimization counts.

The parallel PPO lane executed **1,372 updates, 15,824 minibatch steps and 124,368,632 actor decisions used by completed updates**. Its 5,130 completed training episodes included 38 physical failures in the early exploratory run. A further 98,304 collected decisions were rejected before an update by a C/PyTorch behavior-replay check and are counted separately. Stable PPO runs lowered RMS error while worsening the worst selection peak; none displaced the reward-search winner. On this machine, an actual PPO-update benchmark was **0.555 s on CPU versus 0.184 s on the RTX 3090 including transfer**, approximately **3.02× faster**. Native physical simulation remained on CPU; this is not a claim of a 3× whole-study speedup.

The final budget winner was the reward-selected `history_0p5` attenuation of previously evolved current-history weights. It did **not** receive the final budget evolutionary update. Its direct budget evidence before locking was **20 training cases plus all 28 selection cases**, all passing, with 0.454059 N selection worst error. Other candidates' 84-case audits do not belong to this checkpoint. The checkpoint was frozen before final testing, and neither weights nor selection were changed after seeing those results.

![Development convergence; the earlier stages use the faster reference sensing chain.](figures/development_convergence.svg)

**Final results.** All force scores include startup and every native integration sample. A pass requires completing the recording without a physical stop while remaining within ±0.5 N. The ±7.5 mm travel band is reported separately as the user's preferred operating region; crossing it is different from reaching the physical ±12.5 mm stop.

| Final cohort | Deterministic passes; worst force error | Learned passes; worst force error | Entire recording inside ±7.5 mm, deterministic / learned |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 700 nominal grid cases | 700/700; 0.428526 N | 700/700; 0.418410 N | 700/700 / 700/700 |
| 32 fresh cases | 32/32; 0.483324 N | 30/32; 0.678521 N | 32/32 / 32/32 |
| Four 30 s cases | 4/4; 0.492243 N | 3/4; 0.489666 N before termination | 2/4 / 2/4 |

These are **1,472 scored recordings (736 baseline/policy pairs) and 1,005,340,754 native sample points**. Nine additional native replay recordings, including a reproduced travel-stop failure, are excluded from those unique evaluation counts. The 700-case nominal grid checks parameter coverage; it does not replace the distinct fresh-condition and long-duration tests.

The nominal peak improvement was only 0.010116 N. Mean per-recording RMS error increased from 0.016068 N to 0.040781 N. On fresh cases it increased from 0.027376 N to 0.048349 N. Fresh case 86, at 33 N, S=1.1 kg and 50°, reached 0.678521 N; case 94 also exceeded the limit at 0.501417 N. Neither failure involved contact loss or a travel stop.

![Paired fresh-case force results.](figures/rl_3h_fresh_pairs.svg)
![The worst fresh force recording.](figures/rl_3h_worst_force.svg)
![The separate 700-case nominal grid.](figures/rl_3h_nominal_grid.svg)

In the long 50 N, S=2 kg, 90° case, the learned controller reached the travel stop at **19.13094 s**. Its force remained below 0.5 N until termination, which does not make the recording a pass. The deterministic controller completed all four long recordings but exceeded the preferred travel band in two, reaching 9.028 mm from center. Its worst force reserve was just **0.007757 N**. Neither result supports a claim of comfortable long-duration robustness. There were no software rejections or robot request-clock/gate violations in the final cohorts; obeying the gate alone does not guarantee sufficient recentering.

![Robot travel relative to the preferred band.](figures/rl_3h_robot_travel.svg)
![The learned controller's long-run physical stop.](figures/rl_3h_long_stop.svg)

**Performance limits.** Two additional locked-policy development screens each ran the same 28 cases with both controllers: 112 scored episodes and 3,658,783 actor decisions, with two recovery replays counted separately. They did not alter the final winner.

| Budget-chain development condition | Deterministic passes; worst error | Learned passes; worst error |
|---|---:|---:|
| 50 µs current response, declared sensing timing | 28/28; 0.463682 N | 28/28; 0.454059 N |
| 100 µs current response | 28/28; 0.493979 N | 26/28; 0.640529 N |
| 50 µs current response plus known, matched 50 µs sensing delay | 26/28; 0.513855 N | 15/28; 1.129700 N |

The learned policy also suffered one physical stop with the slower current response and two with added sensing delay. The 100 µs condition's worst force case had **no voltage clipping**, so a higher supply voltage at unchanged current-loop tuning cannot explain away that failure. Added latency remained harmful even when known and matched in identification. These experiments identify current-loop response and synchronized sensor phase as concrete constraints; voltage headroom is only one part of the problem.

![Recorded drive effort and clipping.](figures/rl_3h_drive.svg)
![Paired budget current-response and latency limits.](figures/budget_response_limits.svg)


**Independent implementation checks.** The selected checkpoint's regenerated C source, header, flat weights, layout and arrays match byte for byte; all three cohort launchers verify their locked sources. Two independent normal MATLAB replays then consume the saved requests for fresh cases 86 and 95. Each scores all **1,800,001 samples over 6 s** and exactly reproduces its compiled-run force peak. Across all 27 diagnostic channels, the largest difference is **5.33 × 10⁻¹⁴**, with identical timestamps and no algebraic loops. The 0.678521 N force failure is reproduced. These are plant/sensor/gate replays using recorded actions; they do not substitute MATLAB or PyTorch neural arithmetic for the frozen C actor.


Halving the plant integration step from **3.333 to 1.667 µs**, while preserving the original noise, ADC, actor and robot clocks and replaying the same requests, gives **3,600,001 points**. The worst-case peak changes from **0.678521230 to 0.678507391 N**, a reduction of only **0.000013838 N**; its peak time stays 1.230410 s. The force requirement still fails. This checks recorded-action plant sensitivity, **not closed-loop neural inference with refined feedback states**. No learned branch is promoted on this evidence.
learning_recommendation:
**Recommendation.** Build the budget prototype around the deterministic measured-inertia controller, using the voice coil, upper rigid link and lower opposed spring pair. Retain approximately 19.7 kN/m combined stiffness and 60 N·s/m external damping, and identify the assembled mechanics for each tool. The approximate spring packing remains comfortably within the 100 mm spring-only condition.

Use the budget accelerometer/ADC chain as a **conditional prototype target**: ADXL354-class acceleration sensing, ADS131M08 acquisition at 30 ksample/s, matched 1.9 kHz response envelopes, synchronized force/acceleration measurements and a 10 kHz controller. Target the tested 50 µs current response with at least 32 V usable bipolar output from the proposed 36 V supply. Verify these response and timing figures on the assembled hardware, including filtering, ADC delay, driver phase, calibration and noise; nominal sample rate alone is insufficient.

Before sanding trials, improve and validate sustained robot recentering and establish more force margin than the 0.007757 N long-case reserve. Check thermal operation and structural modes under real sanding vibration. Keep the neural policy as a reproducible research candidate with its failures intact. **Do not deploy it as the flange controller on the evidence obtained here.**


The saved checkpoint, C inference, normalization, exact feature order and locked physics are under `acf_simulink/validation/rl_budget3h_20261005/selected_controller/`. To reproduce the paired 32-case test from the repository root, run:

```bash
/home/tommie/Pesten/puffer4-native/.venv/bin/python acf_simulink/experiments/rl_budget3h_20261005/run_saved_policy.py --cohort holdout32
```

Use `--cohort nominal700` or `--cohort long4` for the other retained tests, and `--dry-run` to verify all source and bank hashes without simulating. The [run guide](/home/tommie/Projects/actuator-model/acf_simulink/experiments/rl_budget3h_20261005/README.md) explains the package and resource needs. The public Simulink model continues to expose the deterministic scientific-reference controller; the research checkpoint has not been promoted into its diagram.

acceleration_update:
##### First PCB within the €100 chip budget

Choose **one ADXL354CEZ (ADXL354C) and one ADS131M08IPBSR** for the planar prototype. Checked single-unit Netherlands distributor prices on 5 October 2026 are €61.71 and €9.45 excluding VAT: **€71.16 excluding VAT, or €86.10 with 21% VAT**. The accelerometer is one three-axis analog chip; the planar model uses two of its outputs. This is the chip subtotal only. [ADXL354CEZ price](https://www.digikey.nl/en/products/detail/analog-devices-inc/ADXL354CEZ/6557313), [ADS131M08 price](https://www.digikey.nl/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/ADS131M08IPBSR/11502308).

Six amplified load-cell bridge channels plus two acceleration axes fill the M08's eight simultaneous channels. The position sensor uses a separately timestamped digital counter. For all three acceleration axes plus six bridges, two M08s give 16 channels; the accelerometer plus two ADC chips totals **€97.54 including VAT** at the same checked prices. Share clock and synchronization and measure inter-device timing. This channel-count option is not a qualification of three-dimensional sanding.

![Accelerometer and ADC chip budget including VAT](figures/rl_budget_chip_cost.svg)

At ±8 g, the reviewed acceleration noise density is **33.75 µg/√Hz** and sensitivity **100 mV/g**. The model converts that density into **0.0186557 m/s² RMS at the fixed reference noise normalization**, then lets the actual filters determine the output noise. The M08 contributes a separate **0.0020898 m/s² RMS** converter-noise injection and an ideal **0.00001403 m/s² code step**. The small code step is not the sensor's usable resolution or bias accuracy. Preserve the post-calibration **±0.005 m/s² bias and ±0.25% scale** targets; gravity tare does not cancel changing thermal bias or dynamic inertia errors. [ADXL354/355 datasheet](https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/adxl354_adxl355.pdf), [M08 datasheet](https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ads131m08.pdf).

The acquisition uses a **7.68 MHz clock and OSR 128 for 30 ksample/s per channel**. Its sinc3 group delay is approximately **49.61 µs**, before the analog chain, transfer, controller latch and computation. The model includes the converter/filter timing; it does not assume zero delay. An instrumentation amplifier with freely chosen cutoff can match channels, but cannot remove the accelerometer's internal dynamics. The ADXL354's nominal 1.9 kHz overall bandwidth is insufficient to establish the complete phase: its internal filter and mechanical response must be measured in the assembled chain.

The budget-chain experiments use a declared **1.9 kHz matched response**, retain the calibrated static/response/timing residuals, and retune the inner current response to **50 µs**. PI + feedforward passes 700 nominal cases, 32 fresh varied cases and four fresh 30 s cases, with respective worst errors **0.428526, 0.483324 and 0.492243 N**. The last reserve is only **0.007757 N**. Adding a known common 50 µs sensing delay makes two of 28 development baseline cases exceed the force limit. These experiments support an affordable bench prototype, but **do not establish the requested good margin with the cheap accelerometer**. The detailed paired neural-controller results below include all failures.

The older ADXL1002 studies explain the benefit of faster sensing; they remain useful reference evidence. The budget decision is an explicit performance tradeoff, not a claim that the ADXL354 preserves their reserve.
acceleration_recommendation: Use **one ADXL354C at ±8 g plus one ADS131M08** for the first planar custom PCB, approximately **€86.10 including VAT for these chips**. Mount the accelerometer rigidly on S, acquire two axes simultaneously with the force bridges and synchronize the S–A encoder. Design accessible filter and clock settings so the installed phase can be measured and the matched response adjusted. Keep the stated bias/scale calibration targets and verify noise with the sander powered. The simulated budget baseline has very little worst-case reserve; accept the hardware only after independent force measurements demonstrate the required margin.
system_recommendation: **Build the first bench prototype with the guided voice coil, upper rigid link, 19.746 N/mm lower opposed spring pair, 60 N·s/m damper, B–S multi-axis load cell and S–A position sensing. Use one ADXL354C plus one ADS131M08 (about €86 including VAT), synchronized 30 ksample/s acquisition, a measured 50 µs current-response target and 10 kHz measured-inertia PI + feedforward with guarded robot recentering. Retain ±7.5 mm as the no-penalty travel band and stop at physical limits. Keep the neural model for research. This is an affordable prototype starting point: the present cheap-sensor model does not establish a good worst-case margin, so require an independent powered-sanding test at ≤0.45 N error including measurement uncertainty before accepting the system.**
top_summary: **Learning and €100 sensing update, 5 October:** one shared recurrent policy now controls full coil-current and robot requests. With the ADXL354C/M08 budget chain, both it and PI + feedforward pass the 700-case nominal grid. The locked neural policy then passes **30/32 fresh varied cases and 3/4 long cases**, with a **0.678521 N force error** and one travel stop. The deterministic baseline passes all **736 physical/force cases**, but its long worst is **0.492243 N** and two long cases leave the accepted ±7.5 mm travel band. Use that baseline for the affordable bench prototype; neither a robust hardware margin nor a deployment-ready neural controller is established.
final_learning_summary: **Final control choice:** retain measured-inertia PI + feedforward. The unified recurrent model was trained, frozen and evaluated; nominal-grid improvement did not generalize to fresh force and sustained-motion tests. The ADXL354C/M08 baseline leaves only **0.007757 N** in its worst fresh long case and exceeds the soft travel band in two long cases. The requested good margin remains a prototype-development target.

#### Recommendation

Use **ADS131M08 at 30 ksample/s per simultaneous channel**, with **7.68 MHz clock / OSR 128**, one ADXL354C and appropriate instrumentation amplifiers on the custom PCB. Six bridge channels plus two acceleration axes fit one ADC. Keep the **50 µs EMA setting, 20 µs post-conversion pipeline and fresh 10 kHz control** in the tested acquisition contract. Measure the complete force and acceleration responses, including the accelerometer's internal dynamics, sinc3 delay, SPI and controller latching. Match their effective timestamps and the estimated surface normal before inertia reconstruction. The instrumentation amplifier cutoff can be selected to achieve this matching; it cannot cancel a sensor's delay. The additional-50-µs experiment below fails two of 28 deterministic development conditions, making timing a demonstrated limitation, not merely a sampling-theory concern.

Retain **±0.01 N force zero, ±0.005 m/s² acceleration bias** and the other tighter calibration targets. At S=2 kg, that acceleration bias already produces 0.01 N inertia error. The cheaper chain passes the new baseline force tests but leaves only 0.007757 N in the worst long recording.
